speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. To help me understand your symptoms, can you tell me if the double vision and weakness have been getting progressively worse over days or weeks? Also, do you experience any muscle pain or dark urine?

speaker: Patient
text: The double vision usually happens when I look up or down, and the weakness in my arms and legs gets worse after activity but improves if I rest. I have not noticed balance problems or numbness.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have any difficulty with swallowing, speaking, or breathing, especially towards the end of the day? I also need to check if your eyelids droop when you look up for a sustained period.

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had recent infections or fevers, and there is no family history of neurological disease. The weakness feels symmetrical in both arms and legs.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Do you experience double vision or eyelid drooping that worsens as the day progresses? I will also request an Acetylcholine Receptor Antibody test to confirm my suspicion.
REQUEST TEST: Acetylcholine Receptor Antibody

speaker: Doctor
text: The presence of Acetylcholine Receptor Antibodies confirms the diagnosis. DIAGNOSIS READY: Myasthenia Gravis
